title: M3.0 Authoring Foundation implementation
purpose: Implement the accepted M3.0 Authoring Foundation as a separate local/offline author application for existing canonical Atlas kits: visual edit, authoritative live validation, author preview, deterministic canonical export and re-import without semantic drift.
invariants: The accepted ATLAS-WP-008 design is normative; implementation may not widen it silently.
Authoring Studio is a separate local/offline application and is not embedded in the learner artifact.
learnit.kit.v2 schema, existing v2/Atlas validators and canonical proof kits are read-only authorities.
M3.0 edits existing valid Atlas kits only; structural add/delete/reorder and new activity types are forbidden.
No-op import/export of each canonical Atlas proof kit is byte-identical.
Semantic edits preserve lineage IDs, allocate required revision IDs once per draft revision, and recompute Atlas claims plus activity/course/package digests.
Authoritative export is blocked until the existing canonical validator stack passes.
Draft persistence uses only the isolated learnit.authoring.m3.v1 namespace and never reads or mutates learner storage.
The local server binds loopback only, enables no permissive CORS and makes no outbound network call.
Preview is author-facing only and cannot claim learner recommendation, memory, transfer or mastery semantics.
No backend, accounts, synchronization, document ingestion, LLM assistance, Gate3, Gate4 or M4+ capability is introduced.
requiredEvidence: Changed paths are exactly a subset of the nine authorized implementation paths.
Both canonical Atlas proof kits load and validate successfully.
No-op export is byte-identical for both canonical proof kits.
Representative QCM and fill semantic edits preserve lineage identities, rotate required revision IDs and produce valid canonical claims/digests.
Repeated export of an unchanged draft is byte-identical and has a stable SHA-256.
Blocking schema/editorial defects disable export and are shown as actionable diagnostics.
Reload restores only authoring draft state; discard clears only the authoring namespace.
Loopback-only server and no-outbound-network behavior are proven.
Edited exports pass the existing general v2 and Atlas editorial validators.
Edited exports are accepted by existing Learn-it import/browser regression without learner source changes.
Product HEAD is frozen exactly before independent QA binding.
adversarialTests: Stale revision IDs or digests after semantic edits.
Stale Atlas claim IDs or stimulus digests.
Duplicate JSON keys, malformed UTF-8 or unsupported canonical values.
Unsupported activity type or phase/role combination.
Export remains enabled despite a blocking canonical diagnostic.
Repeated export differs without a logical draft change.
Server binds non-loopback, enables permissive CORS or attempts external network.
Preview is treated as learner-semantic authority.
Any changed path outside the exact implementation allowlist.
nonGoals: Structural add/delete/reorder of courses, objectives, activities, choices, slots or tokens.
New activity types or contract revision.
Remote publishing, collaboration, accounts or synchronization.
independentReview: QA-WP-018 owns an independent contradictory oracle and never repairs ATLAS-WP-009 files.
Final QA must bind to one exact frozen ATLAS-WP-009 HEAD.
Repository governance and PR-scope checks must pass on the implementation PR.
A short desktop authoring human gate follows independent QA on the exact accepted candidate.
rollback: Revert or drop the isolated authoring/studio implementation, dedicated workflow and package metadata. No learner runtime, learner storage, canonical kit or schema migration is involved.
